extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and KIPO examiners (users of the Korean Patent Act and enforcement rules)
extracted.subtask_description: Official guidance interpreting Korean Patent Act provisions on entitlement, inventorship, succession, protection of legitimate right-holders, required application documents, and offenses concerning confidential patent information. Focused on rules and procedures for filing and prosecuting patent applications in Korea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public officials and scope of divulging confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Public officials refer to ‘employees working for national or regional government agencies under the Act’. Employees of a public corporation equivalent to an administrative institution after individual consideration are deemed public officials. Article 226(2) recognizes executives and employees of a special institution or agency for digitizing patent documents under Article 58 as employees of the Korean Intellectual Property Office and subject to offense for divulging confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies who may be criminally liable for divulging confidential patent information (includes KIPO staff, affiliated institution employees, and certain public-corporation employees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Object of the offense of divulging confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the offense is confidential information on an invention in a patent application acquired in the course of work, including items to be kept confidential under the Patent Act and other relevant acts and items with considerable benefits when kept secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers not only formal classified items but any invention-related information obtained through official duties which would provide considerable benefit if kept secret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of divulgence and misappropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Divulgence means informing a third party of confidential information (includes intentional and accidental divulgence). Misappropriation refers to working an invention in a patent application acquired in the course of work against the right holder's intention or filing a patent/utility model registration with a subservient invention/utility model related to the concerned invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both accidental leaks and deliberate disclosures can constitute the offense; misappropriation includes using the invention or filing legally competing rights derived from confidential access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to a patent (Article 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who makes an invention or his/her successor shall be entitled to a patent: provided, however, that no employee of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or the Korean Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board is entitled to a patent while in office, except by inheritance or bequest. If at least two persons jointly make an invention, they are jointly entitled to a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that inventors (and successors) have original entitlement; KIPO employees are generally barred from obtaining patents while in office; joint inventorship confers joint entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications filed by unentitled persons and protection of legitimate right-holders (Article 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is refused because the application was filed by a person not entitled to a patent (an 'unentitled person'), a subsequent patent application filed by the legitimate right-holder shall be deemed filed on the date of the unentitled person's filing, provided the subsequent application is filed within 30 days after the rejection becomes final and conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a retroactive filing effect to protect legitimate inventors against filings by unentitled parties, but imposes a strict 30-day limit after final rejection of the unentitled application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents granted to unentitled persons and protection (Article 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a trial decision invalidating a patent on the ground of lack of entitlement becomes final and conclusive, a subsequent application by the legitimate right-holder shall be deemed filed at the time the invalidated patent application was filed, subject to the 30-day filing limitation after the trial decision becomes final and conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an already-granted patent is later invalidated for entitlement reasons, the legitimate holder can obtain retroactive priority to the original filing date, but must observe the 30-day rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability and non-pledge of entitlement (Article 37)
rubrics_metrics.description: An entitlement to a patent may be transferable. An entitlement to a patent shall not be pledged. If an entitlement is jointly held, a joint holder may transfer his/her share only with the consent of each joint holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entitlement is transferable but cannot be used as collateral (no pledge). Joint ownership requires co-owner consent to transfer shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession to entitlement — notice and documentary requirements (Article 38 / Procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: If entitlement is transferred after filing, the succession is effective only when a notice of change of the applicant (Annexed Form 20) is filed before registration together with evidential documents proving the ground for change, any necessary permissions/approvals/agreements from third parties, and documents proving representative power if acted by a representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies form numbers and documentary attachments required to make succession effective after filing; one notice can cover multiple applications with identical contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession handling on death, inheritance, and bequest
rubrics_metrics.description: If the person who conducted a proceeding is deceased and entitlement inherited, the proceeding is interrupted; an inheritor must resume by attaching evidential documents of death and inheritance. For all-inclusive bequest, similar documents (death certificate, will) apply; for specific bequest the beneficiary must request the bequest to take over the entitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific documentary evidence (death certificate, family relation certificate, will) required to resume interrupted proceedings after succession by inheritance or bequest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint applications requirement (Article 44)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the entitlement to a patent is jointly held by at least two persons, all entitled persons shall jointly file a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure of all joint owners to join in an application can be a ground for rejection or invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who qualifies as an inventor — substantive contribution standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor is someone who creates technical ideas by using the law of nature and who makes substantial contributions to creation of technical ideas. Examples of those treated as inventors: (Ex1) who newly presents, adds, or supplements concrete conception of ideas to solve technical problems; (Ex2) who embodies or reduces novel ideas to practice through experiment; (Ex3) who provides specific means and methods to achieve purpose and effects; (Ex4) who contributes via concrete advice and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship is a factual, contribution-based test — legal capacity is not required (minors can be inventors) but the contribution must be substantial and concrete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is not an inventor — non-substantial/contributory roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons not treated as inventors include: (Ex1) who simply provides basic technical problems or ideas; (Ex2) who generally manages a researcher; (Ex3) who arranges data and conducts experiments per directions; (Ex4) who supports/entrusts creation by providing funds and equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management, funding, supervision, or routine implementation without contributing concrete inventive concept does not confer inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventorship standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than two persons create an invention, those who jointly made the invention are inventors and entitlement is jointly owned. Each joint inventor must, even partly, make a meaningful contribution to completion through mutual complementation in the technical process; joint owners must be in mutual cooperation for completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires meaningful, collaborative technical contribution; partial, complementary contributions can qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment/correction of inventors during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant unintentionally omitted or misspelled inventors' names, the applicant can add or correct names until an examiner determines patentability. Once an examiner determines patentability, addition of a new inventor shall not be accepted except for incorrect writing or omission occurring during application procedure. Examiners may accept amendments without evidential documents unless special reasons exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds procedural flexibility to correct honest errors before patentability is determined; examiners need not demand proof except where they reasonably suspect intentional misstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner power to order amendment if inventorship suspected not genuine
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner reasonably suspects the person stated as inventor is not the genuine inventor (e.g., inventor not a natural person, minor deemed not to have created invention is listed), the examiner may order amendment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner can act to correct fraudulent or implausible inventorship claims and require applicants to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection measures for legitimate holder filing (procedural requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A legitimate holder seeking protection under Articles 34/35 must file an application in Annexed Form No. 14 to the Commissioner of KIPO, attached with a specification, abstract or drawings, evidential document of the legitimate holder of right, and representation document if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the form and documentary evidence to claim protection; required attachments mirror normal application contents plus evidence of entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of legitimate-holder application — retroactive filing date and patent term calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed by a legitimate holder shall be deemed filed on the earlier date of the unentitled person's filing when conditions are met. Patentability, patent term calculation, and application of relevant provisions for the legitimate-holder application shall be determined based on the initial unentitled filing date. Where a patent is granted to a legitimate holder under Articles 34/35, the term shall be 20 years calculated from the day after the filing date of the application by the unentitled person after registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactive effect affects novelty/prior art and term calculation; example given where third-party intervening filings are rejected because of retroactivity. There are timing limits (see 30-day rules and special timing rules for requests for examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limit for examination requests on legitimate-holder applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the application by a legitimate holder is filed more than three years (five years for applications filed before 2017-03-01) after the initial unentitled filing date, a request for examination can be made within thirty days from the date the legitimate holder filed the application (Article 59(3)). If the request for examination was made at the same time as filing, it is deemed effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows late legitimate-holder applications to proceed provided examination is timely requested within the 30-day window; historical (pre-2017) longer period noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope requirement for retroactivity of legitimate-holder application
rubrics_metrics.description: For the scope of the invention of the legitimate-holder application to be deemed legitimate, the invention disclosed in the description and drawings and the claimed invention must be included in the scope of the invention of the application filed by the unentitled person. If the legitimate-holder application includes inventions not disclosed in the unentitled person's application, the retroactive filing date has no effect for those out-of-scope inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactivity only applies to subject matter that was disclosed in the earlier unentitled filing; new matter in the legitimate-holder filing receives no retroactive priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on applications filed by unentitled persons (examiner actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application was filed by an unentitled person who provided reason for a legitimate-holder's subsequent filing, the examiner shall notify grounds for rejection citing violation of Article 33(1) and make a decision to reject. After a decision to reject becomes final, the examiner shall notify the legitimate holder in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIPO examiners must actively reject unentitled filings and inform legitimate holders; an unentitled person's patent may be invalidated through an invalidation trial if previously granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special succession treatment for multiple applications based on same entitlement (same or different dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more applications relating to the same invention are filed on different dates based on the same succession from the same person, only the applicant of the earlier filing may obtain a patent. If filed on the same date, succession is effective only for the person agreed upon by all applicants after consultation; examiners shall designate a period for consultations and request report; failure to agree results in applications being treated as filed by unentitled persons and rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rules to resolve conflicts where multiple successors file — consultation, time periods, potential measures (e.g., withdrawal of some conflicting applications) and consequences of no agreement (rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required patent application documents (Article 42)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application cover sheet must be filed containing: (1) name and domicile of the applicant (or corporation name/place of business); (2) name and domicile/place of business of an agent if represented (including patent firm name and designated attorney); (3) title of the invention; (4) name and domicile of the inventor. The cover sheet must be accompanied by a specification (description and claims), necessary drawings, and an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the mandatory set of documents for a valid patent filing and the specific information to include on the cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract use limitation (Article 43)
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall be used only for technical information and shall not be used to define the scope of the invention for which patent protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract is informational only and cannot alter claim scope or be used to interpret limits of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application cover sheet content and other indicia
rubrics_metrics.description: The application cover sheet includes applicant name/domicile (or juristic person details), representative/agent details and designated patent attorney if applicable, title of the invention (which must be brief and identical with the specification), name/domicile of inventor, applicant code, priority claim, claim on grace period disclosure exception, and request for examination indication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title should be concise and must match specification; cover sheet must indicate procedural flags (priority, grace period claim, request for examination) to ensure proper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and inventor statements in the cover sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention shall be written briefly and concisely according to the subject matter and shall be identical with that in the specification. An inventor indicated in the cover sheet refers to the actual inventor who has made the invention related to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes consistency of title across documents and factual accuracy of inventor identity.
